event_narrative: Flash flooding along Anderson Creek on CR 50 and CR 52. Depth of water unknown.

Multiple reports from broadcast media of flooding southeast of Miami International Airport. Several vehicles appeared to be stalled on the roadside and temporarily unable to pass, along with the intersection of northwest 41st street and northwest 37th ave under water. Additionally, FDOT reported the two right lanes on SR-836 east beyond Lejeune Road were blocked due to the flooding. Public reported a rain gauge in the area had received 5 inches of rainfall in one hour.
Car submerged on Hwy 72 between Gurley and Paint Rock. Image seen on social media.

A Yavapai County Alert gauge on Black Canyon Creek showed about a two foot rise at 1040 PM.  A downstream gauge (Auga Fria--AFRA3) showed a rise at 200 AM on April 20. The river remained elevated through the evening of May 23.

Showers and thunderstorms with heavy rainfall impacted the affected area during the early evening of July 13. Radar estimates and ground observations indicated between one and a half and three inches of rain fell, leading to a few areas of flash flooding, most notably in the Castleton area along Route 30 near Lake Bomoseen.
Law Enforcement reported several stalled vehicles and water rescues by first responders in town in the past 2 to 3 hours. There was 4 to 5 feet of water reported on many roads and streets.
Heavy rain caused a washout on Porter Hill Road.
Heavy rain caused a washout on Holley Road near Brown Road.
Heavy rain caused a washout on Voter Hill Road in Temple.
